title: Books
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Jenni Romaniuk, Building Distinctive Brand Assets (Oxford University Press, March 2018): a long-term strategy for building and protecting distinctive assets, across asset types such as characters, taglines and jingles; Byron Sharp, How Brands Grow (OUP, 2010); Romaniuk and Sharp, How Brands Grow Part 2 revised (OUP, 2021)

title: Say hello, new logo
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Dated 16 Jan 2019: the original logo used 11 colours and was easy to get wrong; it looked poor on backgrounds other than white, at angles other than its set 18 degree rotation, or with altered colours; versions made to compensate stopped matching; the new logo has a simpler palette and is easier to scale

title: Design & Branding Guidelines
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Partner rules: full logo minimum 70 px digital or 20 mm print, icon minimum 21 px or 6 mm; clear zone half the icon's height; green logo only on black or white, monochrome elsewhere; misuse list (no rotating, stretching, recolouring or adding); avoid over-saturated colours for CMYK print

title: Mailchimp Brand Assets and Resources Guidelines
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Name spelling rules; the wordmark paired with the Freddie character; Cavendish Yellow as hero colour; rules against altering files, implying endorsement, or using the graphics in another business's name; EPS and PNG downloads

title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page updated 4 Oct 2026). 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text at level AA; text in a logo or brand name has no contrast requirement; brand guidelines do not exempt other text

title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.11: Non-text Contrast
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page updated 4 Oct 2026). 3:1 for graphics needed to understand content, such as icons, and for user interface components; logos exempt, with limits when a logo is used as a control

title: OFL-FAQ
supports: Opened with WebFetch. OFL fonts may be used in logos, posters and signage (Q1.1); the resulting artwork is not under the OFL (Q1.1.1, Q1.13); crediting the font is optional (Q1.1.2); fonts cannot be sold on their own (Q1.6, Q3.3); modified fonts must drop any Reserved Font Name (Q3.1)

title: Material Symbols guide
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Variable icon font axes: fill 0 to 1, weight 100 to 700, grade, optical size 20 to 48 dp; 24 px marked as the preferred icon size; Apache License 2.0

title: Define a favicon to show in search results
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Favicon must be square, at least 8 x 8 px, with larger than 48 x 48 px recommended; supported formats; one favicon per hostname; it should represent the brand; the URL should stay stable

title: Google Play icon design specifications
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 512 x 512 px, 32-bit PNG, sRGB, up to 1024 KB, full square; Google Play applies a corner radius of 30% of icon size and a shadow, so assets should not include them; keyline grid for logos; no ranking, deal or misleading text in icons

title: Design Tokens Community Group
supports: Opened with WebFetch. First stable version 2025.10 announced; list of organisations shipping compatible tokens, including Figma, Penpot, Sketch, Style Dictionary, Tokens Studio, Supernova and zeroheight

title: Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Final Community Group Report, 28 Oct 2025: JSON files with .tokens or .tokens.json extensions; $value, $type and $description; groups; aliases with {group.token}; types including color, dimension, fontFamily, fontWeight, duration, cubicBezier, number, border, shadow

title: Search our trademark database
publisher: United States Patent and Trademark Office
supports: Opened with WebFetch (published 30 Nov 2023, updated 8 Apr 2026). Links to the Trademark Search system (tmsearch.uspto.gov), search guides, clearance searching, design search codes and the Trademark ID Manual

title: Likelihood of confusion
publisher: United States Patent and Trademark Office
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The most common reason for refusing registration; marks compared for similarity in sound, appearance, meaning or commercial impression, together with relatedness of the goods or services; examples of related goods; the examiner searches regardless of the applicant's own search

title: Search for a trade mark
supports: Opened with WebFetch. UK searches by trade mark number, owner, keyword, phrase or image, and for flags, emblems and hallmarks; the trade marks journal includes international marks covering the UK

title: Register a trade mark
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The IPO checks for the same or similar existing marks and publishes applications for opposition; registration usually takes around 3 to 4 months without issues; a trade mark lasts 10 years and is renewed every 10 years; cost depends on the goods and services covered

title: Register a trade mark: What you can and cannot register
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A UK trade mark can include words, sounds, logos and colours; it cannot describe the goods, be too common or non-distinctive, be offensive or misleading, be just a generic shape, or use national flags or official emblems without permission

title: Trade marks in the EU
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page last checked 12 Jul 2026). National registration for one country; BOIP for Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg; EUIPO for protection in all EU countries; WIPO for international protection; protection for 10 years, renewable; support from EUIPO and the IP Helpdesk

title: Global Brand Database
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Searches international marks under the Madrid System, Article 6ter emblems and marks from participating national and regional offices, by words, numbers, goods and services, and image similarity

title: Nice Classification
supports: Opened with WebFetch. International classification of goods and services for trade marks; version NCL(13-2026) in force from 1 January 2026

title: Copyright Law of the United States, Chapter 1 (17 U.S.C. 101)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A work made for hire is either work by an employee within the scope of employment, or a specially commissioned work in a closed list of categories when both parties sign a written agreement

title: Copyright Law of the United States, Chapter 2 (17 U.S.C. 201 and 204)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Section 201(b): for a work made for hire the employer or commissioner is the author; section 204(a): a transfer of copyright ownership is not valid without a signed writing

title: How copyright protects your work: License and sell your copyright
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A sale or transfer of UK copyright needs a written, signed assignment; owners can license their work

title: Copyright in the EU
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page last checked 12 Oct 2026). EU copyright is automatic and lasts 70 years after the author's death; licences may be exclusive or non-exclusive and limited by time, territory and use

title: NewsNet Issue 1060: Copyright Office Releases Part 2 of Artificial Intelligence Report
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 29 Jan 2025: prompts alone do not establish authorship of AI output; human expressive elements, creative arrangements or modifications can be protected

title: EU AI Act, Article 50: Transparency obligations
publisher: artificialintelligenceact.eu (Future of Life Institute), text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Disclosure of AI image, audio or video that resembles real people, objects, places or events; lighter duty for evidently artistic or fictional work; applies from 2 August 2026

title: Guide to the Figma MCP server
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Remote server recommended; extracts variables, components and layout; write to canvas in beta on the remote server; available on all plans; writing outside your drafts needs a Full seat; write to canvas free during beta, later usage-based

title: Canva MCP server
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Create and edit designs, search designs and folders, use brand kits and templates, upload assets, export PDF, PNG, JPG, PPTX and MP4, resize, comment

title: zeroheight pricing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Design system documentation platform with a free plan and paid plans; styleguides, token sets, Figma and developer tool connections; an MCP server listed on every plan

title: Design Tokens Color Module 2025.10
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Final Community Group Report, 28 Oct 2025: a colour token's $value is an object with a required colorSpace (such as srgb, display-p3 or oklch) and components, an optional alpha (default 1) and an optional 6-digit hex fallback
